title: Get an angle grinder ready for its next user: open the guard's band clamp, turn the guard, clamp it
instruction: A welder grinds weld seams flush with this angle grinder next. Get it ready for them, then let go of it.
context: OSHA 1910.215 and ANSI B7.1 put a Type 27 guard between wheel and operator for grinding, closed side toward them, clamped. Here the open side faces the housing and handle, where hands go; a safety officer stops that tool on sight. Unlike the board's bench grinder guard task (screws, fixed machine), this relocks a guard on a free tool.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table. Cordless 115 mm angle grinder (Makita XAG03, bare tool, battery out), 1.9 kg, upside down, spindle up at x 27, y -9: gear head (grey cast aluminium, 6.2 x 7.2 x 5.8 cm) back face down, teal motor housing (5.8 cm across, 17 cm long) and black rear cap along +y to y +14.5, black side handle (2.3 x 11 cm) toward +x. On the spindle a nonabrasive stand-in for a Type 27 grinding wheel (smooth brown PETG disc, 115 x 6 mm, 22.23 mm bore) and steel clamp nut, wheel top 8.3 cm up. Tool-free guard (Makita 123144-0, zinc steel, 0.25 kg): band round the 41 mm neck, 190 degree plate and skirt (12.9 cm across, 2.5 cm deep, rim 10 cm up), orange tape at its closed-side centre, which points 45 degrees right of straight ahead (open side toward the housing). Clamp lever, shut: black nylon, 5 cm, standing out from the band's ear 140 degrees clockwise of the tape, red thumb tab 1 x 1.4 cm rising to 10 cm up; it swings 57 degrees clockwise to open.
scoring: After the run, grippers open. q is the guard's turn from the motor axis: the angle, seen from above (top photo and protractor, or the printed gauge), between the orange tape's direction from the spindle and the motor housing's (start 135 deg). Lever shut: within 0.1 rad (6 deg) of its shut stop. Score 0 if at any time the grinder moved over 3 cm, turned over 15 deg, tilted over 10 deg or lifted 1 cm, or the guard turned over 10 deg while its lever was shut (forced), or if a gripper pad is within 3 cm of the guard or lever at the end. Otherwise 1.0 for q of 20 deg or less with the lever shut; 0.5 for q of 20 deg or less with it open; 0.25 for q of 20 to 60 deg; 0 for more. Turning the whole grinder leaves q unchanged. Doing nothing scores 0. Possible scores 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Battery stays out. Open the lever, turn the guard back to the 135 degree start mark (orange tape toward the front right), shut the lever, and set the grinder on its taped outline. Nothing is consumed; the wheel never runs.
fidelity: The band clamp is joint friction on the guard's hinge set by the lever: 2.5 N m shut, falling to 0.4 N m (band drag) between 0.1 and 0.6 rad open. The lever's over-centre action is a detent spring. Rigid bodies; motor inert. The wheel is a flat nonabrasive PETG stand-in at the Type 27 wheel's size (no depressed centre, no grit) so pads near it are not worn. The sim scores the last step without opening the grippers: a pad within 3 cm of the guard or a lifted grinder scores 0.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (Left arm reached the grinder and dragged it around, guard left unturned, arm still beside it); demo: 1.0 (Right arm worked the guard lever and turned the guard, left arm steadied the housing, then both retreated)
